newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mixed, Sep up on deliveries, China.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mixed, Sep up on deliveries, China.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby September higher on light deliveries plus news wheat destined for China had been inspected recently at U.S. export ports, traders said.
"They were surprised China showed up in the inspections," a trader said.

USDA Tuesday said U.S. wheat inspected for export during the week ended August 29 totaled 25.241 million bushels with 2.425 million bushels of the tally destined for China. The market was knocked lower this summer partly by news that China cancelled some purchases.
China reportedly cancelled the orders due to some disease problems in U.S. wheat shipments.

September wheat found support on the posting of 20,000 bushels of wheat Tuesday against the September contract, which was less than the trade expected. Also, deliveries were lighter than expected Friday at roughly 400,000 bushels. There were ideas last week that three million to five million bushels of wheat may be posted on the September.
Wheat closed four cents higher to 4-1/4 lower, with September up four at $4.52-1/2 a bushel.
Other months closed lower on bull spreading. News of the U.S. air strike on Iraq lent minor pressure, traders said.
"We're not selling wheat to Iraq but if it (conflict) escalates I suppose it could be a problem," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Cargill Inc and The Chicago Corp each bull spread 500,000 bushels of September/December, traders said. SAK Trading bought two million bushels of December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 14,000, up from 11,879 contracts Friday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, Merrill Lynch Futures bought 150 December $4.40 puts and sold 150 December $5.00 calls, pit sources said. Prudential Securities bought 150 December $4.40 puts and sold 150 December $5.00 calls.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 3,000, up from 2,539 Friday.
